# Read a run's record or export from a program

<!-- description: The run record's types, the evidence entry's, and the functions that read a run's phase and an entry's sources. -->

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-library-reference.mjs from the API reports and the built declarations; do not edit by hand: after `npm run build`, run `npm run docs:library`. -->

A run's record (`RunRecord`) is one object that holds everything Realm knows about the run, and `realm run export` writes all of it into a bundle. `deriveRunPhase` gives a run's phase from its record, and `outputSourceOf` and `readSupplier` say where an evidence entry's output and supplier came from. A record written before Realm recorded how a run ended has no `sealed_by`: `classifyLegacySeal` gives the arm it would have carried, and `armToOutcome` the outcome an arm means. This page lists the record's types, the evidence entry's, and those functions.

Where the docs teach it: [Run record and export bundle format](../run-record-and-export.md).

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`armToOutcome`](#armtooutcome) | function | `arm -> outcome class`. |
| [`classifyLegacySeal`](#classifylegacyseal) | function | Classify a terminal record written before `sealed_by` existed into the arm it would have carried. |
| [`classifyModelFailure`](#classifymodelfailure) | function | Says what a failed model request needs before it can succeed, from the request's own values only. |
| [`outputSourceOf`](#outputsourceof) | function | Where an evidence entry's output came from: `{ source }` when the entry carries `output_source`, else `{ absent_cause }`, the first `OUTPUT_SOURCE_ABSENT_CAUSES` member that holds. |
| [`readSupplier`](#readsupplier) | function | The supplier of an evidence entry's input or output: its recorded role, or why it names none. |

| [`CACHE_AUTO_BASES`](#cache_auto_bases) | const | On what `--prompt-cache auto` chose a request's cache lifetime (`UsageRecord.cache_auto.basis`). |

| [`CACHE_CONTROL_FIELDS`](#cache_control_fields) | const | The cache fields Realm itself adds to a request: Anthropic's `cache_control` markers and OpenAI's `prompt_cache_key`; the closed set a recorded refusal names. |

| [`CACHE_MARKED_PARTS`](#cache_marked_parts) | const | What carried a cache marker, or OpenAI's key, on one request (`UsageRecord.cache_marked`). |
| [`CACHE_MISS_TYPES`](#cache_miss_types) | const | Anthropic's reasons a request's cache read fell short, and `unknown` for a reason Realm does not know, recorded as such and never verbatim (`CacheMissReason.type`). |
| [`CACHE_REFERENCE_SOURCES`](#cache_reference_sources) | const | Where a request's copied predecessor came from: `run` (this run's record) or `earlier_run` (another run's) (`CacheReference.from`). |

| [`CACHE_REQUESTS`](#cache_requests) | const | What Realm asked a provider to cache on a request, as stored (`UsageRecord.cache_requested`). |

| [`OUTPUT_SOURCE_ABSENT_CAUSES`](#output_source_absent_causes) | const | Why an evidence entry carries no `output_source` (`outputSourceOf`'s `absent_cause`). |
| [`OUTPUT_SOURCES`](#output_sources) | const | Where a bare `auto` step's recorded output came from (`EvidenceSnapshot.output_source`). |
| [`PRINCIPAL_ABSENCES`](#principal_absences) | const | Why a door names no principal (`Principal`'s `absent`). |
| [`REQUEST_ENDPOINTS`](#request_endpoints) | const | Which kind of address a request went to: the provider SDK's default (`default`) or another one (`custom`) (`UsageRecord.endpoint`). |
| [`SEAL_ARMS`](#seal_arms) | const | Every way a run can be sealed, as a closed list read at run time (`SealedBy.arm`). |
| [`SEAL_DOORS`](#seal_doors) | const | The commands and tools that end a run on request: `realm run abandon`, the MCP `abandon_run` tool and `realm run cleanup` (`SealedBy.door`). |
| [`SUPPLIER_ABSENT_CAUSES`](#supplier_absent_causes) | const | Why an evidence entry names no supplier. |
| [`SUPPLIER_ROLES`](#supplier_roles) | const | The parties that supply a step's input or output, as an evidence entry records them (`EvidenceSnapshot.supplied_by`). |

## Functions

### armToOutcome

function · public

`arm -> outcome class`. Total, exhaustive, no default. NOT read by `deriveEffectiveTriggers`
(which keeps its own `mintOutcome` — the two may diverge by design); this exists for readers
that need the class from a STORED record.

```ts
function armToOutcome(arm: SealArm): 'complete' | 'fail' | 'abort' | 'abandon';
```

### classifyLegacySeal

function · public

Classify a terminal record written before `sealed_by` existed into the arm it would have carried.
Returns `undefined` when the record cannot be placed — callers must then refuse to
fabricate (`deriveRunPhase` falls back to the pre-#367 ladder; the future migrate vehicle buckets
it `unclassifiable` and exits 1).

A READ-PATH function, not only a migration function: an unhealed record reached through
`store.get()` never passes through any sweep, so this is a PERMANENT oracle and correctness never
depends on a migration having run.

Structure (design rev 3 §4 + Amendment 1 defect 4): MARKERS AS A HINT, PROSE REACHABLE WITHOUT
THEM. Markers are checked first when present (they are the strongest legacy signal, and the
legacy ladder gives them precedence), but every prose-identifiable arm is classifiable from
`terminal_reason` alone, because the only external store has no marker columns. That leaves just
the two genuinely prose-less arms — `guard_abort` (reason-less by construction) and
`abandon_requested` (free-text reason) — marker-dependent.

```ts
function classifyLegacySeal(run: ClassifiableRun): SealArm | undefined;
```

### classifyModelFailure

function · public

Says what a failed model request needs before it can succeed, from the request's own values only.
It returns `transient` (another try can fix it), `setup` (an operator must fix something first),
`permanent` (it will fail the same way again), or `null` when it cannot place the failure (gap 2,
unit i-a). The rules run in this order, and the first that applies wins:
1. Realm code `MCP_TOOL_NOT_FOUND` or `MCP_TOOL_NAME_COLLISION`: `setup`, in any phase.
2. Phase `mcp_discovery`: `null` (not a model call).
3. Phase `after_response`: `permanent`.
4. Class `validation_rejected`: `null` (it stays on the schema-retry path).
5. `x-should-retry: true`: `transient`, at any status.
6. A workspace refusal, 401, 402, 403, 404, class `sdk_missing`, or a used-up quota, credit or spend
   limit (OpenAI's codes `insufficient_quota`, `credit_balance_exhausted`,
   `organization_spend_limit_exceeded`, `project_spend_limit_exceeded`,
   `organization_usage_limit_exceeded`, or the type `insufficient_quota`; Anthropic's type
   `billing_error`): `setup`.
7. `x-should-retry: false`: `permanent`, at any status.
8. 408, 409, 429 or 5xx, or class `connection_error`, `connection_timeout` or `aborted_by_budget`:
   `transient`.
9. 400, 413 or 422: `permanent`.
10. Anything else: `null`.
A phase outside the three is not placed (`null`).

```ts
function classifyModelFailure(facts: ModelFailureFacts): ModelFailureKind | null;
```

### outputSourceOf

function · public

Where an evidence entry's output came from: `{ source }` when the entry carries `output_source`,
else `{ absent_cause }`, the first `OUTPUT_SOURCE_ABSENT_CAUSES` member that holds.
`definition` is the run's workflow, when the reader has it. `realm run inspect` renders
it; a reader of an export, which writes the record as stored, derives the absence with it too.

```ts
function outputSourceOf(entry: Pick<EvidenceSnapshot, 'step_id' | 'kind' | 'output_summary' | 'output_source'>, definition: Pick<WorkflowDefinition, 'steps'> | undefined): {
    source: OutputSource;
} | {
    absent_cause: OutputSourceAbsentCause;
};
```

### readSupplier

function · public

The supplier of an evidence entry's input or output: its recorded role, or why it names none.
`engine_input` for an entry whose input the engine built (any step that is not an agent step),
`not_recorded` for an agent step's entry written before the field.

```ts
function readSupplier(entry: Pick<EvidenceSnapshot, 'supplied_by' | 'step_id' | 'kind'>, definition: Pick<WorkflowDefinition, 'steps'> | undefined): {
    role: SupplierRole;
} | {
    absent: SupplierAbsentCause;
};
```

## Interfaces

### AnswerFacts

interface · public

A recorded answer's route as its door declared it, and what showed a form
(`EvidenceSnapshot.answer`).

```ts
interface AnswerFacts {
    route: string;
    shown?: {
        renderer: string;
    };
    channel_evidence?: ChannelEvidence;
}
```

### Attributed

interface · public

A program's name, how that name is known, and the host's channel. Not a person; not a process.

```ts
interface Attributed {
    by: string;
    by_source: BySourceClass;
    channel: string;
}
```

### CacheAuto

interface · public

A request's `cache_auto`: the basis of the `auto` choice, the gaps it read, and where its prices
came from. `prices` is absent when no price was needed (no kept gap).
Normalised where it enters the record (`normalizeCacheAuto`).

```ts
interface CacheAuto {
    basis: CacheAutoBasis;
    gaps_s?: number[];
    prices?: CacheAutoPrices;
}
```

### CacheControlsRejected

interface · public

A custom endpoint answered 400 naming a cache field Realm added, and a retry without the cache
fields worked (`UsageRecord.cache_controls_rejected`).
`proven` is `cache_fields` when the request that worked
dropped only the cache fields, `none` when it also dropped strict (#311's ladder ran on the retry's
400). What the provider said stays in the verbatim error facts (`api_param`, `api_code`, #313).

```ts
interface CacheControlsRejected {
    status: 400;
    dropped: 'cache_fields'[];
    proven: 'cache_fields' | 'none';
    fields: readonly CacheControlField[];
}
```

### CacheMissReason

interface · public

Anthropic's reason for a cache miss, with its approximate token count when given.

```ts
interface CacheMissReason {
    type: CacheMissType;
    cache_missed_input_tokens?: number;
}
```

### CapabilityBlock

interface · public

The marker on a step that the program which last tried it could not run, because its handler or
adapter was not registered there, keyed by step name (`RunRecord.capability_blocks`).
Written when an auto step's handler/adapter is NOT REGISTERED in the executing runner's registry: the
step settles RECOVERABLY (removed from `in_progress_steps`, claim omitted, NOT added to `failed_steps`,
run NOT terminal-sealed) so a correctly-provisioned runner can reclaim it. Advisory metadata for
DETECTION and operator diagnostics ONLY — the four step sets stay authoritative for eligibility, so a
stale marker (step since completed on another runner) self-suppresses via the eligibility cross-check in
`findCapabilityBlockedSteps`. Clearing it on recovery is hygiene, not correctness. Additive-optional (the
`claims` / `extension_identity` precedent): legacy records lack it; JSON-file-store-only until external
stores round-trip unknown optional RunRecord fields through update().

```ts
interface CapabilityBlock {
    requirement: {
        kind: 'handler' | 'adapter';
        name: string;
    };
    code: string;
    at: string;
}
```

### ChannelEvidence

interface · public

The account a channel's door says sent an answer, as the channel reports it
(`AnswerFacts.channel_evidence`).

```ts
interface ChannelEvidence {
    team?: string;
    user: string;
    ts?: string;
    thread_ts?: string;
}
```

### ClaimRecord

interface · public

A step's claim, as the run keeps it while the step is being run: its deadline, its token and the
program that holds it (`RunRecord.claims`).
Written atomically when a step is claimed.

```ts
interface ClaimRecord {
    deadline: string | null;
    token?: string;
    holder?: Attributed;
    since?: string;
    lease?: {
        id: string;
    };
}
```

### DriveFailureRecord

interface · public

One failed attempt to drive a step: when, which step and provider, what kind of failure, and its
message (`DriveFailuresField.entries`).
A "drive attempt" is realm trying to advance a step —
not only a provider call: an auto step whose validation rejects the submission wedges the run
identically and is recorded here too.

Before this record existed, every one of these failures wrote NOTHING to the store. The console
said what happened, the process exited, and the run read healthy on every operator surface until
`never_claimed_idle` noticed it 24 hours later.

```ts
interface DriveFailureRecord {
    at: string;
    step: string;
    provider: string;
    error_class: 'connection_timeout' | 'connection_error' | 'api_status' | 'sdk_missing' | 'validation_rejected' | 'aborted_by_budget' | 'startup_failure' | 'other';
    message: string;
    evidence_count?: number;
    gate_id?: string;
    attempts_sdk?: number;
    elapsed_ms: number;
    declared_per_attempt_ms?: number;
    derived_ceiling_ms?: number;
    last_observed_status?: number;
    retry_after_observed_ms?: number;
    usage?: UsageRecord[];
    model_text?: DriveFailureModelText;
    model_attempts?: ModelAttempt[];
}
```

### DriveFailuresField

interface · public

A run's recent drive failures: the last few, plus the total and the time of the first, which do
not reset when the oldest is dropped (`RunRecord.drive_failures`).

`entries` holds at most 5, MOST-RECENT-LAST. `total` and `first_failed_at` live OUTSIDE the ring
deliberately — a run that failed forty times must not read as though it failed five, and the
moment trouble started is the one fact a ring cannot preserve.

```ts
interface DriveFailuresField {
    first_failed_at: string;
    total: number;
    entries: DriveFailureRecord[];
}
```

### EvidenceSnapshot

interface · public

One evidence entry of a run's record (`RunRecord.evidence`): what one step run or one answered
question recorded, with its times, its input and output, its status and its hash.

```ts
interface EvidenceSnapshot {
    step_id: string;
    started_at: string;
    completed_at: string;
    duration_ms: number;
    input_summary: Record<string, unknown>;
    output_summary: Record<string, unknown>;
    status: 'success' | 'error' | 'skipped' | 'abandoned';
    error?: string;
    evidence_hash: string;
    attempt?: number;
    kind?: 'execution' | 'gate_response';
    gate_message?: string;
    responded_by?: string;
    driven_by?: Attributed;
    answer?: AnswerOnRecord;
    client_prompt_requested?: true;
    principal?: Principal;
    output_source?: OutputSource;
    supplied_by?: SupplierRole;
    claim_proof?: GateClaimVerdict;
    admitted_by?: AdmittedBy;
    resolution?: 'expired_default' | 'expired_abort';
    diagnostics?: StepDiagnostics;
    agent_profile?: string;
    agent_profile_hash?: string;
    tool_calls?: ToolCallRecord[];
    model_text?: ModelText;
    model_attempts?: ModelAttempt[];
    resolved_params?: Record<string, unknown>;
    warn?: string;
    debug_output?: unknown;
    trace?: TraceEntry[];
    trace_digest?: string;
    trace_summary?: TraceNormalizationSummary;
    effective_timeout_seconds?: number;
    clipped_to_ms?: number;
    exhausted_by?: 'attempts' | 'total_timeout';
    error_code?: ErrorCode;
    error_category?: ErrorCategory;
    agent_action?: AgentAction;
    stop_reason?: 'no_retry_policy' | 'total_timeout' | 'non_retryable' | 'attempts';
}
```

### ModelAttempt

interface · public

One failed try of one of a step's model requests, as `model_attempts` keeps it on an evidence entry
and on a drive-failure entry. Numbers, closed words and `null` only: never a text, never usage
(gap 2, unit i-a).

```ts
interface ModelAttempt {
    request: number;
    kind: ModelFailureKind | null;
    error_class: DriveFailureRecord['error_class'] | null;
    status: number | null;
    wait_ms: number | null;
    retry_after_ms: number | null;
    exhausted_by?: 'attempts' | 'total_timeout';
    then?: 'gateway' | 'cache_probe' | 'strict_ladder';
}
```

### ModelFailureFacts

interface · public

The values `classifyModelFailure` reads from one failed model request. A value that is absent,

interface · public

A SHA-256 (64 lowercase hex) of each part a request sent: `system`, and `tools`, `prompt` and

```ts
    format?: string;
```

interface · public

```ts
interface StepDiagnostics {
```

### StructuredOutputMeta

interface · public

What a step's attempt under `structured_output: 'strict'` records about strict mode: only what
Realm can observe, never whether the provider enforced it (`EvidenceSnapshot.structured_output`).
Deliberately carries NO `applied`
field (unwitnessable — a silently-stripping proxy could accept `strict` on the wire and never
honor it; `sent` only ever claims "realm placed strict on the request handed to the SDK", never
that the API enforced it). Per-attempt: a retry-configured step's evidence array can carry a
different value per attempt. `requested` is always `true` when this object is present at all —
it exists ONLY on a step that declared `structured_output: 'strict'`.

SCOPE (issue #311 truth pass): every field on this object EXCEPT `tool_args` describes ONE
dimension — the step's own OUTPUT request (the submit tool realm sends for the step's answer).
That was the only dimension #236 shipped, so the original wording did not need to say so;
it does now. `tool_args` describes the independent TOOL-ARGUMENTS dimension, and the two
legitimately disagree on the same attempt: a tools-bearing step is permanently
`sent: false` / `unsupported_context_tools` at the OUTPUT level while simultaneously carrying
genuine per-tool `strict_sent: true` entries under `tool_args`. When reading a single field,
check which dimension it belongs to before concluding "strict was off".

```ts
interface StructuredOutputMeta {
    requested: true;
    sent?: boolean;
    caveats?: string[];
    downgrade_reason?: 'gate_ineligible' | 'api_rejected_schema' | 'grammar_unavailable' | 'service_unavailable' | 'provider_unsupported' | 'unsupported_context_tools' | 'external_agent' | 'compat_endpoint';
    api_message?: string;
    api_param?: string | null;
    api_code?: string | null;
    provider?: 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'openai-reasoning' | `module:${string}`;
    submission_channel?: 'tool' | 'text';
    tool_args?: {
        tools: Array<{
            name: string;
            strict_requested: true;
            strict_sent: boolean;
            reasons?: string[];
            caveats?: string[];
        }>;
        dropped_mid_attempt?: {
            reason: string;
            api_message?: string;
            api_param?: string | null;
            api_code?: string | null;
            strict_turns_before_drop: number;
        };
    };
}
```

### CacheAutoBasis

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_AUTO_BASES`: what `--prompt-cache auto` based a request's chosen cache

type · public

### CacheAutoPrices

type · public

Where the `auto` choice took its prices: the runner's price file (`economics`), or none, with the
cause (`CacheAuto.prices`). From the price file, the one lifetime it could not cost is excluded.
Closed-set words only: no model id, no path.

```ts
type CacheAutoPrices = {
    from: 'economics';
    excluded?: [
        'short'
    ] | [
        'long'
    ];

        CacheAutoRate

    missing?: CacheAutoRate[];
```

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_AUTO_RATES`: a price-file rate the `auto` choice reads, as a `missing`

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_CONTROL_FIELDS`: a cache field Realm itself adds to a request, as
`CacheControlsRejected.fields` names the ones a custom endpoint refused.

```ts

```

### CacheDiagnostics

type · public

A request's question to Anthropic about a cache miss, and its answer
(`UsageRecord.cache_diagnostics`). One of three shapes: it did not ask because Anthropic refused
the question in this drive; it asked with no earlier message (a call's first request); or it
named an earlier answer, with what came back.

```ts
type CacheDiagnostics = {
    asked: false;
    cause: 'rejected';
} | {
    asked: true;
    reference_id: null;
} | {
    asked: true;
    reference_id: string;
    result: CacheDiagnosticsWord | CacheMissReason;
};
```

### CacheDiagnosticsWord

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_DIAGNOSTICS_WORDS`: what Anthropic said in words about a cache miss,
for a request that named an earlier answer.

```ts
type CacheDiagnosticsWord = (typeof CACHE_DIAGNOSTICS_WORDS)[number];
```

### CacheMarkedPart

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_MARKED_PARTS`: a part of a request that carried a cache marker, or
OpenAI's key (`UsageRecord.cache_marked`).

```ts
type CacheMarkedPart = (typeof CACHE_MARKED_PARTS)[number];
```

### CacheMissType

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_MISS_TYPES`: Anthropic's reason a request's cache read fell short
(`CacheMissReason.type`).

```ts
type CacheMissType = (typeof CACHE_MISS_TYPES)[number];
```

### CacheReference

type · public

A copy of a request's predecessor, the same step's previous request, kept when it is not an
earlier entry of the same stored list (`UsageRecord.reference`). It is the first request of the
step's last call on the run's record, or the same step's first request in another run
(`earlier_run`).
`from` says where it was found,
`request_start` is required, and each other field but one is the predecessor's own, copied when it
had one; `cache_requested` says whether it asked the provider to cache (piece A-1b). The one
exception is `agent_profile_changed` (piece C3), which is no field of the predecessor: `true` when
the step's agent profile differs between the two requests and both are known, worked out where the
copy is made, and absent otherwise. `prefix_sha256` is not copied (it equals
`prefix_parts.prompt` on both providers). Never a `reference` of its own, never a `request_index`
(an index is not identity, #715 (R)), never a `request_in_call` (the copy is always a call's first
request).

```ts
type CacheReference = {
    from: CacheReferenceSource;
} & Pick<UsageRecord, 'request_start'> & Partial<Pick<UsageRecord, 'request_id' | 'provider' | 'model' | 'endpoint' | 'cache_requested' | 'cache_read_input_tokens' | 'cache_creation_input_tokens' | 'cache_write_tokens' | 'cache_creation' | 'cache_lifetime_s' | 'cache_ttl_sent' | 'cache_auto' | 'prefix_chars' | 'prefix_parts' | 'cache_marked' | 'request_strict_sent'>> & {
    agent_profile_changed?: true;
};
```

### CacheReferenceSource

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_REFERENCE_SOURCES`: where the copy of a request's predecessor was
found, in this run or an earlier one (`CacheReference.from`).

```ts
type CacheReferenceSource = (typeof CACHE_REFERENCE_SOURCES)[number];
```

One of the words in `CACHE_REQUESTS`: what Realm asked a provider to cache on a request, as
stored (`UsageRecord.cache_requested`).

```ts
type CacheRequest = (typeof CACHE_REQUESTS)[number];
```

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_REQUEST_SOURCES`: whether a request's cache setting was stated with

```ts
type CacheRequestSource = (typeof CACHE_REQUEST_SOURCES)[number];
```

type · public

One of the words in `CACHE_STATES`: a step's cache state, judged per direction from what the

type · public

The record shape both legacy classifiers read.

```ts
type ClassifiableRun = Pick<RunRecord, 'terminal_state' | 'failed_steps' | 'terminal_reason' | 'aborted_at' | 'abandoned_at'>;
```

### DriveFailureModelText

type · public

The text of the model requests one drive failure covers, on its entry
(`DriveFailureRecord.model_text`). It is the evidence entry's `ModelText`, with
`dropped_messages`: the number of messages left out to keep the entry within its budget. A
request that got no answer has `request_id: null` and `reply: null`; an answered request's
`request_id` is the id of its record in the entry's `usage`.

```ts
type DriveFailureModelText = (Extract<ModelText, {
    recorded: true;
}> & {
    dropped_messages?: number;
}) | Extract<ModelText, {
    recorded: false;
}>;
```

### GateClaimVerdict

type · public

A verdict with a cause that does not belong to it does not compile.

```ts
type GateClaimVerdict = {
    proof: 'matched' | 'absent' | 'mismatch';
} | {
    proof: 'unverifiable';
    cause: 'no_claim' | 'claim_has_no_token' | 'store_keeps_no_claims';
} | {
    proof: 'spent';
    cause: 'answered' | 'expired';
};
```

### ModelFailureKind

type · public

What a failed model request needs before it can succeed: one of `MODEL_FAILURE_KINDS`.

```ts
type ModelFailureKind = (typeof MODEL_FAILURE_KINDS)[number];
```

### ModelText

type · public

The text of each model call made for a step, on its evidence entry
(`EvidenceSnapshot.model_text`). `realm agent` and `realm listen` write it; a program that embeds
the engine can pass its own in `StepMeta.modelText`.

`recorded: true` holds the texts. `messages` holds each distinct message once, and `tools` each
distinct tool list (the request's tools as JSON). `realm agent` and `realm listen` mask each text
for known secret values (`hidden` counts what that mask hid), then cut it at 64 KB of UTF-8 on a
code-point boundary (`cut` gives the bytes kept and the text's full size). The engine stores a
`StepMeta.modelText` as it is given: it neither masks nor cuts it. Each of `requests` names what
one request sent and what came back by their places in `messages`, its tool list by its place in
`tools`, and carries its `request_id` (the id of its entry in `diagnostics.cache.requests`).

A message's text is its parts in order with no separator: a text part as it is; any other part
as compact JSON, of a tool part's `type`, `id`, `tool_use_id`, `tool_call_id`, `name`, `input`,
`content` and `is_error`, of a thinking part's `type` and `thinking`, of any other part's `type`.
Cache marks, signatures and the data of a redacted thinking part are not kept.

`recorded: false` says why a step Realm drove has no texts: recording was switched off
(`--no-record-model-text`), or the provider module reported none it could read.

```ts
type ModelText = {
    recorded: true;
    messages: Array<{
        role: 'system' | 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool';
        text: string;
        cut?: {
            kept_bytes: number;
            full_bytes: number;
        };
        hidden?: number;
    }>;
    tools: Array<{
        json: string;
        cut?: {
            kept_bytes: number;
            full_bytes: number;
        };
        hidden?: number;
    }>;
    requests: Array<{
        request_id: string | null;
        sent: number[];
        tools?: number;
        reply: number[] | null;
    }>;
} | {
    recorded: false;
    why: 'switched_off' | 'provider_did_not_report';
};
```

type · public

One of the words in `OUTPUT_SOURCES`: where a bare `auto` step's recorded output came from

## Constants

### BY_SOURCE_CLASSES

const · public

How a program's name is known. `stated` — a host passed an explicit name; `ambient` — the
operator set `REALM_OPERATOR`; `derived` — the OS user and host name. `verified` (#603) and
`capability` (#597) are added by the units that produce them.

```ts
const BY_SOURCE_CLASSES: readonly [
    "stated",
    "ambient",
    "derived"
];
```

### CACHE_AUTO_BASES

const · public

On what `--prompt-cache auto` chose a request's cache lifetime (`UsageRecord.cache_auto.basis`).
The bases:
- `no_measurement` — produced by the CLI's `resolvePromptCache` for the setting `auto`, which the
  adapter writes on a request that carries no choice of its own (a host that passes none): no gaps
  were measured, so the runner's prior is asked for (caching 3-M D-3: older records too);
Caching 3-M (D-2): the other three are produced by the CLI's `chooseStepCaches`, one choice per
agent step, which `realm agent` passes on each of the step's calls:
- `step_gaps` — a step without tools, chosen by the provider's rule over the gaps between the
  step's requests in the workflow's earlier runs (`stepCacheGaps`; possibly none — the runner's
  prior is then asked for);
- `step_gaps_unreadable` — the read of the earlier runs failed; the runner's prior is asked for and
  the drive goes on;
- `tool_step` — a step that calls tools, on Anthropic: its own turns reuse the entry, so the short
  lifetime is asked for whatever its gaps.

```ts
const CACHE_AUTO_BASES: readonly [
    "no_measurement",
    "step_gaps",
    "step_gaps_unreadable",
    "tool_step"
];
```

### CACHE_AUTO_PRICE_CAUSES

const · public

Why `--prompt-cache auto` chose without prices (`CacheAuto.prices.cause`, with `from: 'none'`).
Each member's producer:
- `no_file` — `runner.cache.economics` is not set (the CLI's `readAutoPrices`);
- `economics_unreachable` — the file could not be read (`readCacheEconomics`);
- `economics_unreadable` — the file is not a valid price file (`readCacheEconomics`);
- `model_unknown` — the file has no entry for the requested model (`selectEconomicsRates`);
- `input_zero` — the row prices input at 0, or at no finite positive number
  (`chooseAutoLifetime`, row 3);
- `rate_missing` — the row has no read rate, or no write rate for either lifetime
  (`chooseAutoLifetime`, row 4; `missing` names them); #896 unit B: for a provider with one
  lifetime, no read rate or no `cache_write` (`chooseAutoOneLifetime`).

```ts
const CACHE_AUTO_PRICE_CAUSES: readonly [
    "no_file",
    "economics_unreachable",
    "economics_unreadable",
    "model_unknown",
    "input_zero",
    "rate_missing"
];
```

### CACHE_AUTO_RATES

const · public

The price-file rates the `auto` choice reads, in the order a `missing` list names them (the price
file's own order).
#896 unit B: `cache_write`, the one write rate of a provider with one
lifetime (OpenAI). Anthropic's `missing` names only `cache_read`, `cache_write_5m` and
`cache_write_1h`; OpenAI's only `cache_read` and `cache_write`.

```ts
const CACHE_AUTO_RATES: readonly [
    "cache_read",
    "cache_write",
    "cache_write_5m",
    "cache_write_1h"
];
```

### CACHE_BASES

const · public

How a cache number is known: reported by the provider, or not observable
(`StepCacheDetail.basis`).
Never a zero standing in for an absence.

PR 1a ships exactly TWO members: `'provider_reported'` and `'unobservable'`. Nothing in this PR
DERIVES a cache number (it reads what the provider reported, or records that it could not see) —
so a `'derived'` member would be a declared member with no producer, and a type consumer would
reasonably believe realm derives these numbers today. `'derived'` arrives in the PR that derives
something (a vocabulary ships its producers with it — the same rule every const in this PR obeys).

```ts
const CACHE_BASES: readonly [
    "provider_reported",
    "unobservable"
];
```

### CACHE_CONTROL_FIELDS

const · public

The cache fields Realm itself adds to a request: Anthropic's `cache_control` markers and OpenAI's
`prompt_cache_key`; the closed set a recorded refusal names.
Normalised at the write: any other name drops the fact.

```ts
const CACHE_CONTROL_FIELDS: readonly [
    "cache_control",
    "prompt_cache_key"
];
```

### CACHE_DIAGNOSTICS_WORDS

const · public

What Anthropic said in words for a request that named an earlier answer: `no_divergence`,
`pending` or `not_returned`. `no_divergence`: it found none; `pending`: it has not worked it out
yet; `not_returned`: the answer carried nothing Realm can read.

```ts
const CACHE_DIAGNOSTICS_WORDS: readonly [
    "no_divergence",
    "pending",
    "not_returned"
];
```

### CACHE_MARKED_PARTS

const · public

What carried a cache marker, or OpenAI's key, on one request (`UsageRecord.cache_marked`). The
parts: the `system` text and the prompt's head block (Anthropic's markers, and OpenAI's marks on
GPT-5.6 and later), or OpenAI's `key`.
Caching 3-M (A-0): or the `conversation` so far — the marker Anthropic's tool
main turns put on a copy of the last message (#899).

```ts
const CACHE_MARKED_PARTS: readonly [
    "system",
    "prompt",
    "key",
    "conversation"
];
```

### CACHE_REFERENCE_SOURCES

const · public

Where a request's copied predecessor came from: `run` (this run's record) or `earlier_run`
(another run's) (`CacheReference.from`). `run`: the first request of the same step's last call
there, from an earlier drive; `earlier_run`: the same step's first request there.
Normalised at the write: any other word drops the reference.

```ts
const CACHE_REFERENCE_SOURCES: readonly [
    "run",
    "earlier_run"
];
```

### CACHE_REQUEST_SOURCES

const · public

Where a request's cache setting came from: `stated` (`--prompt-cache` was given) or
`runner_default` (the runner's own default) (`UsageRecord.cache_requested_source`).
Produced by
the CLI's `resolvePromptCache` and written by the Anthropic adapter it is handed to.

```ts
const CACHE_REQUEST_SOURCES: readonly [
    "stated",
    "runner_default"
];
```

### CACHE_REQUESTS

const · public

What Realm asked a provider to cache on a request, as stored (`UsageRecord.cache_requested`). The
words: `off` (asked for nothing; the Anthropic adapter with `--prompt-cache off`, or `auto`
choosing off), `lifetime` (asked for a cache lifetime; the Anthropic adapter with `short`,
`long`, or `auto` choosing one), `provider_rules` (realm asks for nothing and the provider's own
caching rules apply; the OpenAI and o1 adapters; with `cache_key_sent`, realm also sent a cache
key).
#896: the OpenAI adapter on GPT-5.6 and later at OpenAI's own address records `lifetime` (30
minutes) or `off` for a single-shot request, and `off` for a tool step's requests under `off`.

```ts
const CACHE_REQUESTS: readonly [
    "off",
    "lifetime",
    "provider_rules"
];
```

### CACHE_STATES

const · public

The words a step's cache state takes (`StepCacheDetail.state`).

Observation is per DIRECTION (read, write), never per object. `'never_engaged'` and
`'write_only'` each make a claim about BOTH directions, so each is mintable only when both were
reported; a provider that reports one counter and withholds the other yields
`'partially_observed'`, because there is no true four-word answer for that data and forcing one
would be the very coercion `CACHE_BASES` forbids one level up.

```ts
const CACHE_STATES: readonly [
    "engaged",
    "never_engaged",
    "write_only",
    "partially_observed",
    "unobservable"
];
```

### MODEL_FAILURE_KINDS

const · public

What a failed model request can need before it succeeds: another try (`transient`), an operator's
fix first (`setup`), or nothing, because it will fail the same way again (`permanent`). An
operator's fix is a key, a permission, a model name, a workspace, credit or an MCP tool.
`classifyModelFailure` files a failure into one of them from the failure's own values (gap 2,
unit i-a).

```ts
const MODEL_FAILURE_KINDS: readonly [
    "transient",
    "setup",
    "permanent"
];
```

### OUTPUT_SOURCE_ABSENT_CAUSES

const · public

Why an evidence entry carries no `output_source` (`outputSourceOf`'s `absent_cause`). The first
that holds, in this order (whether a step is bare needs its definition, so the definition's absence
is asked before bareness):
 - `not_an_output_entry`: the entry records no step output — a `gate_response` entry (the answer,
   or the expiry that settled the question) or the reclaim audit entry (`output_summary.reclaimed`);
 - `definition_unavailable`: the workflow given has no step by the entry's name (or none was given),
   so whether the step is bare cannot be said;
 - `not_a_bare_step`: the step has a handler or a service, or is not an `auto` step — its output is
   its own, and the field is never written for it;
 - `predates_output_source`: a bare `auto` step's entry written before the field existed.

```ts
const OUTPUT_SOURCE_ABSENT_CAUSES: readonly [
    "not_an_output_entry",
    "definition_unavailable",
    "not_a_bare_step",
    "predates_output_source"
];
```

### OUTPUT_SOURCES

const · public

Where a bare `auto` step's recorded output came from (`EvidenceSnapshot.output_source`).
A bare `auto` step has no handler and no service.
 - `driven_step`: what the caller that named the step returned through its dispatcher;
 - `dependency`: its single `depends_on` step's recorded output (the engine ran it);
 - `run_params`: the run's params (the step has no `depends_on`);
 - `none`: nothing to copy, so the step recorded `{}` — the engine ran a step that depends on more
   than one step, or whose single dependency has no successful entry (a trigger rule let it run
   after that step failed or was skipped).

```ts
const OUTPUT_SOURCES: readonly [
    "driven_step",
    "dependency",
    "run_params",
    "none"
];
```

### SEAL_ARMS

const · public

Every way a run can be sealed, as a closed list read at run time (`SealedBy.arm`). The type
`SealArm` derives from it (the `STOP_KINDS` pattern: the const array is the runtime
enumeration). One value per terminal seal-site function-branch in the 21-path census.

APPEND-ONLY (the Tekton lesson, design rev 3 §3): an arm's meaning never changes; changed seal
behaviour mints a NEW arm. That rule is what keeps every stored `sealed_by.arm` decodable
forever, and what makes a future #378 resolution land as a mapping/arm ADDITION rather than as
a rewrite of stored records.

```ts
const SEAL_ARMS: readonly [
    "complete",
    "gate_resolution_complete",
    "guard_pass_complete",
    "gate_expiry_default",
    "step_failure",
    "guard_resolution_error",
    "spawn_failure",
    "extensions_load_failure",
    "handler_abort",
    "guard_abort",
    "gate_expiry_abort",
    "abandon_requested",
    "cleanup_sweep"
];
```

### SEAL_DOORS

const · public

The commands and tools that end a run on request: `realm run abandon`, the MCP `abandon_run` tool
and `realm run cleanup` (`SealedBy.door`).

`@remarks` Recorded beside the program that used them. Like the seal arms, the list only grows.

```ts
const SEAL_DOORS: readonly [
    "realm_run_abandon",
    "abandon_run",
    "realm_run_cleanup"
];
```

Why an evidence entry names no supplier.

const · public

The parties that supply a step's input or output, as an evidence entry records them
(`EvidenceSnapshot.supplied_by`).
PR-0's producer is the agent's answer to an agent step; a door
through which an operator supplies an engine step's input adds `operator` with it (the membership

```ts
const SUPPLIER_ROLES: readonly [
    "agent"
```

## Also used by this job

Names this job reaches whose entry is on another page.

- [`AgentAction`](write-a-handler.md#agentaction): What an agent does next, decided by the engine (`WorkflowError.agentAction`).
- [`AuthGithub`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#authgithub): GitHub HMAC-SHA256 hex body signature (header 'X-Hub-Signature-256').
- [`AuthHmac`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#authhmac): Generic HMAC body signature with a configurable header / algorithm / encoding.
- [`AuthNone`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#authnone): Documented, discouraged escape hatch — accept without verification (trusted network / localhost only).
- [`AuthSharedSecret`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#authsharedsecret): Header-token auth — the request carries a user-configured header equal to a shared secret.
- [`AuthStripe`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#authstripe): Stripe timestamped HMAC body signature (header 'Stripe-Signature').
- [`ContextWrapperFormat`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#contextwrapperformat): The wrapper format Realm puts around a `{{ workflow.context.<name> }}` reference in a template (`WorkflowDefinition.context_wrapper`).
- [`DedupConfig`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#dedupconfig): How a webhook trigger drops a repeated event: the dot-path to the event's id, how long an id is remembered, and what to do when the id cannot be read (`WebhookTrigger.dedup`).
- [`deriveRunPhase`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#deriverunphase): Derives the `run_phase` from the run record's fields.
- [`ErrorCategory`](write-a-handler.md#errorcategory): The broad kind of failure a `WorkflowError` reports: network, an outside service, the run's state, invalid input, the engine itself, or a resource (`WorkflowError.category`).
- [`ErrorCode`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#errorcode): Every code a `WorkflowError` can carry, grouped by its category; a reply's error and the error catalogue name it (`WorkflowError.code`).
- [`ExecutionMode`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#executionmode): The kinds of step a workflow declares in `execution`: `auto`, `agent`, `guard` and `finalizer` (`StepDefinition.execution`).
- [`ExtensionIdentityEntry`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentityentry): One point-in-time identity of the extension code executing a run.
- [`ExtensionIdentityModule`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentitymodule): One loaded extension module's identity.
- [`ExtensionIdentitySignals`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentitysignals): Labeled advisory signals — each independently fail-soft; never part of the comparison.
- [`ExtensionIdentityTree`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentitytree): Versioned deterministic directory-tree fingerprint over the module roots.
- [`FilterCondition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#filtercondition): One condition of a webhook trigger's filter: a header or a dot-path into the payload, and the value it must equal or the values one of which it must equal; a request that fails a condition is ignored.
- [`FinalizerTrigger`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#finalizertrigger): Terminal outcome(s) a finalizer step matches.
- [`GateConfig`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#gateconfig): A gate's settings: its choices, who may answer, its messages, its timeout and what happens when it expires, and its reminders.
- [`InputMapNode`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#inputmapnode): One node of a step's `input_map`: a dot-path string, a `$literal` value, or an object of further nodes (`StepDefinition.input_map`).
- [`JsonSchema`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#jsonschema): The JSON Schema object a workflow gives for a step's input and for a run's params (`StepDefinition.input_schema`, `WorkflowDefinition.params_schema`).
- [`LiteralNode`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#literalnode): A node in an input_map tree.
- [`McpServerConfig`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#mcpserverconfig): An MCP server a workflow's tool-enabled steps may call: its id and the command that starts it (`WorkflowDefinition.mcp_servers`).
- [`ProtocolConfig`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#protocolconfig): A workflow's own words for the agent protocol: a quick-start paragraph that replaces the generated one, and rules added as they are written (`WorkflowDefinition.protocol`).
- [`RateLimitConfig`](write-a-handler.md#ratelimitconfig): How fast Realm calls a service: requests per second, the burst it allows, and how long it waits after a 429 (`ServiceDefinition.rate_limit`).
- [`RetryConfig`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#retryconfig): How a step is tried again after a failure: the most attempts, the backoff and its delays (`StepDefinition.retry`).
- [`ServiceDefinition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#servicedefinition): A service a workflow declares under `services`: the adapter that calls it, its trust, and its rate limit (`WorkflowDefinition.services`).
- [`ServiceTrust`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#servicetrust): The words a workflow's `services: <name>: trust:` takes (`ServiceDefinition.trust`).
- [`StepDefinition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#stepdefinition): One step of a workflow, as the loaders return it under `WorkflowDefinition.steps`: what it does, how it runs, the steps it waits for, and its input and settings.
- [`TemplateDefinition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#templatedefinition): A named reusable step group with parameter placeholders.
- [`TemplateParam`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#templateparam): A single parameter declaration in a template.
- [`TriggerDefinition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#triggerdefinition): What starts a workflow's runs from outside; today a webhook is the only kind (`WorkflowDefinition.trigger`).
- [`TriggerFilter`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#triggerfilter): Post-normalisation form (loader converts shorthand → { all: [...] }).
- [`TriggerRule`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#triggerrule): Controls when a step becomes eligible based on its dependencies' outcomes.
- [`TrustLevel`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#trustlevel): The words a step's `trust` takes: `auto`, or `human_confirmed` and `human_reviewed`, which open a gate a person answers (`StepDefinition.trust`).
- [`WebhookAuth`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#webhookauth): How a webhook trigger checks that a request is genuine: a shared secret, GitHub's or Stripe's signature, an HMAC, or none (`WebhookTrigger.auth`).
- [`WebhookTrigger`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#webhooktrigger): A workflow's webhook trigger: the path it answers, how it checks requests, which requests it takes, how it drops repeats, and how it maps a payload to run params.
- [`WorkflowContextEntry`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#workflowcontextentry): A single named entry in the workflow_context section.
- [`WorkflowDefinition`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#workflowdefinition): A workflow as the loaders return it: its id, name and version, its params schema, its steps, and its services, protocol and trigger when it has them.
